actions.description: Command one or more actuated joints to target positions in joint space, optionally over a declared duration, and report whether the target was reached within tolerance.

inputs.description: Target angles of the two joints in rad: the head angle and the lift arm angle
inputs.name: joint_positions

actions.name: move_joints

facts.text: Client is the protocol client and high-level API class of the library
The client starts with the head at its minimum angle and the lift at its minimum height
RobotState packets update the reported pose, head angle, wheel speeds, lift position, battery voltage, acceleration, gyro and status
robot_picked_up and robot_moving follow the picked-up and wheels-moving events the client handles
set_head_angle sends a SetHeadAngle packet with the angle in radians
set_lift_height sends a SetLiftHeight packet with the height in millimetres
The minimum head angle is -25 degrees and the maximum is 44.5 degrees
The minimum lift height is 32.0 mm and the maximum is 92.0 mm
The lift arm is 66.0 mm long and its pivot point is 45.0 mm above the ground
The minimum and maximum lift arm angles are asin((height - pivot) / arm length) of the minimum and maximum heights
LiftPosition builds a height from an arm angle as sin(angle) * arm length + pivot height and reports the angle of a height back
The head is controlled with the DriveHead and SetHeadAngle messages and its angle is read from the head_angle_rad field of RobotState, whose head_in_pos status flag says whether it is in position
The lift is controlled with the DriveLift and SetLiftHeight messages and its height is read from the lift_height_mm field of RobotState, whose lift_inpos status flag says whether it is in position
The head motor is stopped with the StopAllMotors message
The README connects a robot with Client(), start(), connect() and wait_for_robot(), and disconnects and stops it afterwards
The README warns that the project is a tool for exploring the robot, unstable and heavily under development
